content:
We are announcing Lax (laxarchive.org), an open archive that pairs Lean formalizations with natural language mathematics.

Lax presents definitions and statements in both natural language and Lean, allows users to judge these formalizations, and records the checked proofs and assumptions behind them. Submissions are independent, citable contributions.

Compared to other Lean archives, like Palomar and Lean Pool, Lax differs in two ways

  • composition: Lax submissions can build on top of each other.
  • presentation: Lax allows authors to augment their papers side-by-side with Lean formalizations.
    This makes Lax entries well suited to accompany submissions to conferences or journals.

We invite you to an online meeting on Lax and its uses. We will discuss

  • how to formalize your results with AI agents (via Lax’s CLI),
  • how Lax can help you as an author or reviewer,
  • what to find on Lax’s website.

The workshop will be held on 30 Sept 2026 10:00 - 11:30 CET, consisting of one hour of presentation and demos and half an hour of discussion. No Lean or AI experience is required. We kindly ask participants to register under laxarchive.org/workshop

We are building Lax for the math/tcs community. If you have suggestions for improvements, please reach out to us at lax.lean.archive@gmail.com or join us at discord

Édouard Bonnet (CNRS, ENS Lyon, LIP)
Jan Dreier (HPI Potsdam)
Clemens Kuske (HPI Potsdam)
